objects_built.name: require_manager
objects_built.role: Loads the logged-in user by $auth.id and stops with accessdenied unless role is manager or admin. Called first by refund approval and price change endpoints.

objects_changed.name: me PATCH
objects_changed.change: Removed role from input; replaced data = $input[""] with an explicit field list (name, phone, marketing_opt_in).

objects_changed.name: refunds/{refund_id}/approve POST
objects_changed.change: Added tag manager-only; function.run require_manager as first statement.

objects_changed.name: products/{product_id}/price PATCH
objects_changed.change: Added tag manager-only; function.run require_manager as first statement.

templates_considered: no_self_promotion (AUTH-030): fits the role-escalation half of the ask; used unchanged except fields narrowed to role.
admin_endpoints_check_role (AUTH-002): did not fit; it selects by admin path or tag, and the ask's endpoints are not admin endpoints.
role_based_access recipe: did not fit as a whole; it is built around admin endpoints and a role field check, not manager-only write endpoints. Its AUTH-030 part is the same as no_self_promotion.

rules.covers: A signed-in user cannot write their own role through request input (me_PATCH).
Any object writing refunds or products must call require_manager before the write, including future endpoints.
The refund approval and price change endpoints call require_manager as their first statement.

ask_parts_not_covered.part: issue_refund AI tool can refund payments without a manager
ask_parts_not_covered.why: couldn't tell how: a tool has no $auth, so require_manager cannot run inside it; the right fix is a product decision

ask_parts_not_covered.part: Staff can view (read-only) refunds and products
ask_parts_not_covered.why: no check exists for read access

ask_parts_not_covered.part: Who holds the manager role, and how it is granted or revoked

ask_parts_not_covered.why: not in the ask beyond refunds, prices and role; no check reads runtime authorisation of other writes

assumptions: manager role name is exactly "manager"; "admin" also allowed (ask says managers only; flagged to customer).
Price change means writes to the products table; refund approval means writes to the refunds table.
Staff can already view refunds and products via existing GET endpoints (refunds_GET, products_GET), so no change was needed there.
confusions: The brief says to write the policy 'naming the objects you build', but the policy params have no clear way to scope to a function by name beyond functions:[...]; it was not obvious whether the function name must match the stored XanoScript name exactly. Used function name require_manager.

The role_based_access recipe and admin_endpoints_check_role template assume a shared admin path or tag. Nothing in the skill covers a non-admin role gate on arbitrary endpoints; I had to compose stack.statement_order and object.statement_required by hand.

The no_self_promotion template's fields example includes is_admin, which does not exist in this workspace; it produced a 'field not on any table' warning. The template gives no guidance on dropping fields that do not exist.

The stack.statement_order params doc says tables selects objects reaching a table, not just objects writing it. It was not clear whether reaching includes read-only endpoints (it does, and they pass since they have no after statement). Worth stating in the check description.
Function call syntax in the workspace is function.run <name> { input = {...} } as $x; for a function taking no input I passed input = {}. Unverified whether an empty input is required.
wished_for: A template or recipe for 'only role X may run these endpoints' that is not tied to admin paths.
A way for an AI tool to carry an authenticated user (or to be scoped to a role) so guards can apply to tools as well as endpoints.
Guidance on handling template fields that name objects absent from this workspace.
why_confidence: Policies parse and the dry run is clean, and the role field escalation and the two manager-only endpoints are covered. Confidence stops short of high because the issue_refund tool is outside what the policy can enforce, role assignment is outside the workspace, and the checks read definitions only, so a real manager check at run time is not proven by a policy.
